clue.text: Cook demeans rich stock

indicators.note: to cook is to doctor or falsify, as with cooked books, so the letters are tampered into a new order

blocks.note: the eleven letters of the two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to prepare a rich broth that is somehow beneath them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' and 'stock' together suggest a kitchen, but stock here is a shop's goods and 'Cook' is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop's stock is the goods it holds for sale, which is exactly what its wares are called.

clue.text: Line the setter’s rejected is really bad

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back where it came from, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for line
the setter refers to himself as I, so 'the setter has' becomes I'VE

explanation.surface: A setter has thrown out a line of verse because it was truly dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's in a crossword is the setter's own I, and the 's stands for 'has', giving I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wicked or morally wrong is about as bad as a thing can be, an intensified sense of badness.

clue.text: Rotters Charlie notices

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
advertisements are notices put up to inform the public

explanation.surface: Some scoundrels spot a man named Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notices' reads as a verb, but it is the noun for public announcements.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotter and cad are both old-fashioned British terms for a man who behaves dishonourably, especially towards women.

clue.text: A constant call for praise

blocks.note: taken as written
c is the scientific symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
to claim something is to call for or demand it as a right

explanation.surface: Someone is always demanding compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'call for praise' as one phrase, but the definition stands alone at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclaim is enthusiastic public approval, a strong synonym for praise as either noun or verb.

clue.text: Show affection towards female creature taking time

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a doe is a female deer or rabbit
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An animal lover makes time to fuss over a female pet.
explanation.walkthrough: DOTE is usually followed by 'on', and 'towards' plays that role in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To dote on someone is to lavish fond, often excessive, affection upon them.

clue.text: Trap in small recess set by former monarch

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a nook is a small recess or corner
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A trap has been laid in an alcove built by a king or queen of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set by' only places the monarch after the recess. ER is Elizabeth Regina, so since 2022 a former monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To snooker someone is to leave them stuck with no good move, from the cue game, so to thwart or trap them.

clue.text: Stage manager and journalist showing common sense

blocks.note: a stage of a game or process is a level
the head is the person in charge
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A theatre's stage manager and a reporter are both behaving sensibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage manager' looks like one theatre job, but the two words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone level-headed stays calm and makes sound, sensible judgements, which is what having common sense amounts to.

clue.text: Petty officer, setter and nan consumed fruit

blocks.note: PO is the naval abbreviation for petty officer
the setter refers to himself as me
nan and gran are both informal words for a grandmother
to consume food is to eat it, past tense ate

explanation.surface: A sailor, the puzzle's author and someone's grandmother have eaten some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Nan is everyday British for grandmother, so it converts to GRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The pomegranate is a round red fruit packed with juicy seeds, so it is one example of fruit.

clue.text: Main character is that woman with nothing

blocks.note: her is the pronoun for that woman
O looks like zero, or nothing

explanation.surface: A story's lead is a woman who has nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies a female lead, which fits the pronoun piece but not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of a novel or film is its central figure, the protagonist the story follows.

clue.text: Start of victory sign for defence

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
a sign is an indication of something

explanation.surface: A team's early win signals a strong defence.
explanation.walkthrough: The sporting picture of victory and defence is a decoy; defence is the argument that clears someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A vindication is a justification or defence that clears someone of blame or proves them right.

clue.text: Used to be number one around end of December

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps another
the end of a word is its last letter, so only that one is taken

blocks.note: number one is a nursery euphemism for a wee, urinating
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone was formerly top of the charts at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: Number one suggests the Christmas chart, but it is the childish word for passing water.
explanation.definitionFit: Were is a past form of the verb to be, so it serves as 'used to be' in a sentence like 'they were happy'.

clue.text: Men loved pet running into building site

indicators.note: running suggests things moving about loosely, so the letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: the eleven letters of the three words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A beloved dog escapes and dashes onto a construction site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running into' reads as one phrase about the pet; 'running' is the shuffle signal and 'into' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A development is a new housing or commercial estate under construction, so a site where building is happening.

clue.text: Warning of anger then it dissipated

indicators.note: something dissipated is dispersed and scattered, so the letters break apart and regroup

blocks.note: the eleven letters of the three words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A sign of rage appeared, and then the mood blew over.
explanation.walkthrough: Warning is used as an adjective here, as in a warning look.
explanation.definitionFit: A threatening gesture or sky signals danger ahead, so it gives a warning of something unpleasant to come.

clue.text: Show former love greeting Chip

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
hi is a casual greeting
a chip is a small piece or bit

explanation.surface: An old flame says hello to a man called Chip, all on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chip' is capitalised to look like a name, but it is a small fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhibit is to put on display publicly, as a gallery does, so it is a synonym for show.

clue.text: Wait with sailor above line

blocks.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A seaman is told to linger above the waterline.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'above' puts the sailor first. A railway line is RY.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is an old-fashioned verb for lingering or delaying, which is to wait around.

clue.text: Storm possibly battered haw tree

indicators.note: something battered is knocked out of shape, so the letters are bashed into a new order

blocks.note: the seven letters of the two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A gale may have beaten up a hawthorn tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' tells us a storm is just one example of the answer. A haw is the berry of the hawthorn.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm is one kind of atmospheric condition, so it is an example of the broader category, conditions outdoors.

clue.text: Best terrace erected on street

indicators.note: something erected is raised upright, and in a down entry raising letters makes them read upwards

blocks.note: a terrace is a row of joined houses
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: The finest row of houses has been built on a particular road.
explanation.walkthrough: Best reads as an adjective, but it is the verb meaning to beat, which is the opposite-looking answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone and to worst someone both mean to defeat them; the verbs are synonyms despite the adjectives being opposites.

clue.text: Bloke with old river house

blocks.note: a bloke is a man
O is the abbreviation for old
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A man owns an old house by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloke is everyday British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is a large country house with its lands, so a grand kind of house.

clue.text: Looked at and followed orders missing first two items

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the opening pair of letters is dropped

blocks.note: to follow orders is to obey them, past tense

explanation.surface: Someone inspected a list and did as instructed, but the first two items on it were missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'items' sounds like things on a list, but it means the letters of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it closely, so eyed is the past tense of looked at.

clue.text: Chief is impatient on and off

indicators.note: on and off describes something intermittent, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: The boss gets restless from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on and off' looks like it describes the boss's moods, but it picks the even letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Main and chief both mean principal or most important, as in the main reason or the chief reason.

clue.text: Hold good tool

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a rasp is a coarse file used for shaping wood

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep a firm hold of a decent tool.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'good tool' as a phrase, but each word is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp is to seize and keep something firmly in the hand, a synonym of hold.

clue.text: Look around English lake initially locating graceful creature

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one piece wraps the others
initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: to gaze is to look steadily
E is the abbreviation for English
L is the abbreviation for lake
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone scans an English lake to spot an elegant animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' follows lake but applies to locating; lake gives L by its usual abbreviation. GAZE then wraps E, L, L.
explanation.definitionFit: The gazelle is a slender, swift antelope famed for its elegance, so it is a fair example of a graceful animal.

clue.text: Triumphant ombudsman’s hiding illusion

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it concealed inside, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A victorious complaints official is concealing some deception.
explanation.walkthrough: An ombudsman is an official who investigates public complaints; here the word just supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantom is something seen or imagined that has no real existence, so it is an illusion or apparition.

clue.text: Defeat in unpopular drama

blocks.note: out means out of fashion, no longer popular
a play is a drama

explanation.surface: A failure in a play nobody liked.
explanation.walkthrough: Defeat looks like a noun about a flop, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To outplay an opponent is to perform better than them in a game and so beat them.

clue.text: At that point England’s capital is overwhelmed by menace

indicators.note: a capital is the head letter of a word, so only the first is used
to be overwhelmed is to be engulfed, so one piece is swallowed by another

blocks.note: a menace is a threat
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: At a certain moment, London was swamped by danger.
explanation.walkthrough: England's capital looks like London, but it is just the letter E. THEREAT is an archaic word for thereupon.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereat is a formal, old-fashioned adverb meaning at that place or at that time, so at that point.

clue.text: Fix chess pieces close to board

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is used

blocks.note: chess pieces are called men
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone sets the chess pieces near the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' reads as nearby, but it means the end letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend something broken is to repair it, a plain synonym of fix.

clue.text: Leaders of Leeds United despairing over game

indicators.note: leaders go in front, so the first letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: the opening letters of the three words
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Leeds United's managers are in despair after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds United is an English football club. 'over' reads as 'about', but it is the cricket over.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a simple board game played with dice and coloured counters, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Mark swinging regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A man named Mark goes swinging often.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a name, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark and a sign can both be a symbol or indication showing something, as a sign of respect.

clue.text: Clever and sweetly pleasing

blocks.note: first meaning: shrewd or ingenious
second meaning: attractive in an endearing way

explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' looks like it joins two qualities of one person, but it separates two meanings of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both shrewd or quick-witted, especially in American use, and attractive in a charming, endearing way.

clue.text: Noble, ailing American twice welcomes band

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: ailing means unwell, ill
US is short for American, written out twice
a trio is a band of three musicians

explanation.surface: A sick American aristocrat repeatedly greets a group of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The two US pieces sit either side of the band.
explanation.definitionFit: Illustrious means distinguished and highly respected, close to noble in the sense of grand and admirable.

clue.text: No amount of touching in north-east

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

blocks.note: NE is the abbreviation for north-east
on means touching, as resting on a surface

explanation.surface: Nobody in the north-east gets any physical contact at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No amount of touching' reads as one phrase, but the definition ends before 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: None means not any, so zero quantity of something, which is exactly no amount.

clue.text: Endorsed mermen doc Ed shot

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: the eleven letters of the three words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A film-maker named Ed shot a documentary about mermen, and it got approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doc Ed shot' suggests filming a documentary; 'shot' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse something is to give it public approval and support, which is to recommend it to others.
